title: Collective Dynamics in Spin Chains with Constrained Dissipation: Classically Fragile but Quantum Robust
authors: Pietro Brighi, Gianluca Frazzei, Igor Lesanovsky, Juan P. Garrahan, Alberto Biella
abstract: Collective non-equilibrium phenomena in many-body systems are strongly influenced by fluctuations, particularly in the vicinity of phase transitions, where the interplay between classical and quantum effects can alter cooperative behavior. Here, we investigate this classical-quantum competition in a kinetically constrained spin chain, the dissipative far-East model. In absence of fluctuations, the system exhibits emergent collective dynamics, resulting in phase coexistence. We find that this phenomenon is robust to quantum fluctuations, which further stabilize it, whereas classical fluctuations suppress phase coexistence at long times. We map out the steady-state phase diagram using a cluster mean-field approach and characterize the dynamics with stochastic tensor-network methods. Within the bistable phase we identify signatures of dynamical heterogeneity in both the local magnetization and the entanglement dynamics. This highlights how competing quantum fluctuations and classical kinetic constraints shape the relaxation dynamics and the phase structure of many-body systems.
summary: This research analyzes collective dynamics in a dissipative spin chain, demonstrating how the interplay between quantum and classical noise dictates the system's phase structure. The authors find that while quantum fluctuations can stabilize complex, bistable phases, the introduction of classical noise destroys this collective behavior. The study employs advanced theoretical tools like Cluster Mean-Field theory to map out these non-equilibrium phase boundaries.
main_problem: The paper investigates the competition between classical and quantum fluctuations in determining the collective dynamics and phase structure of many-body systems near phase transitions.
main_result: The system exhibits collective dynamics that are robust to quantum fluctuations (maintaining bistability) but are suppressed and eliminated by the introduction of classical fluctuations.
method: The study employs a combination of Cluster Mean-Field theory, stochastic tensor-network methods, and analysis of quantum jump unravellings.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum dissipative spin chain, specifically the far-East model (fEM), whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating both coherent Hamiltonian evolution and constrained dissipation.
key_observables: Local magnetization ($m_\alpha$), entanglement dynamics, bistability order parameters ($\Delta m_z$, $\Delta J$), and relaxation time ($	au$).
important_parameters: Dissipation strength ($\gamma$), transverse field ($\Omega$), bias ($\delta$), and classical fluctuation strength ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes approximations such as the Cluster Mean-Field ansatz and relies on analyzing the steady-state solutions of the master equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing hysteresis (bistability) in magnetization ($\Delta m_z$) and emission rates ($\Delta J$) when quantum fluctuations are present, contrasting this with the disappearance of hysteresis when classical fluctuations are introduced.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and the general competition between fluctuation types. It then uses Mean-Field and Cluster Mean-Field approaches to map the phase diagram, demonstrating bistability. Finally, it focuses on the role of classical noise, showing its destructive effect on the quantum-stabilized collective dynamics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium phase transitions and the role of noise (both classical and quantum) in shaping the steady-state structure, which is central to modern statistical mechanics and open quantum systems.
